summary.en: The traps that sink most new businesses, and how to spot them early.
summary.bs: Zamke koje potapaju većinu novih biznisa i kako ih rano uočiti.

concepts.youtubeQuery: top reasons why startups fail CB Insights

en.one: Most start-ups fail for a handful of repeated reasons: no real market need, running out of cash, the wrong team, being out-competed, or pricing and cost problems.
en.explain: Studies of failed start-ups (like those by CB Insights) keep finding the same top causes. Knowing them helps you check your own business against them regularly, before it's too late.
en.example: A smart-home gadget start-up spends two years perfecting its product, launches to little interest, and runs out of money in four months. Both 'no market need' and 'ran out of cash'.
en.why: Learning from others' failures is far cheaper than learning from your own.
en.mixup: Failure is rarely about one bad day. It's usually a slow build-up of warning signs that were ignored.

bs.one: Većina start-upa propadne iz nekoliko ponavljajućih razloga: nema stvarne potrebe na tržištu, nestane novca, pogrešan tim, nadjača ih konkurencija, ili problemi s cijenama i troškovima.
bs.explain: Istraživanja propalih start-upa (npr. CB Insights) stalno nalaze iste glavne uzroke. Poznavanje tih uzroka ti pomaže da redovno provjeravaš svoj biznis prema njima, prije nego bude kasno.
bs.example: Start-up za pametne kućne uređaje dvije godine usavršava proizvod, lansira ga uz malo interesa i ostane bez novca za četiri mjeseca. I 'nema potrebe na tržištu' i 'nestalo je novca'.
bs.why: Učenje iz tuđih neuspjeha je mnogo jeftinije nego iz vlastitih.
bs.mixup: Propast je rijetko jedan loš dan. Obično je to sporo gomilanje znakova upozorenja koji su ignorisani.

en.one: Premature scaling is growing too fast, by hiring, opening locations or spending on ads, before the business model is proven.
en.explain: Growth multiplies whatever you have. If customers aren't staying or each sale loses money, growing faster just loses money faster. Prove the basics on a small scale first: customers return, unit economics are positive, and operations work.
en.example: A burger shop is busy for three months and opens two more locations with a loan. The first one's popularity was mostly novelty, and the new locations lose money every month.
en.why: It's one of the most common causes of start-up death, even for businesses with a good idea.
en.mixup: Being busy isn't the same as being proven. Check whether the numbers work before multiplying them.

bs.one: Premature scaling (prerano širenje) je prebrz rast, zapošljavanjem, otvaranjem lokacija ili trošenjem na oglase, prije nego je poslovni model dokazan.
bs.explain: Rast umnožava sve što imaš. Ako kupci ne ostaju ili svaka prodaja gubi novac, brži rast samo brže gubi novac. Prvo dokaži osnove u malom: kupci se vraćaju, ekonomija po jedinici je pozitivna, a poslovanje radi.
bs.example: Burger radnja je puna tri mjeseca i otvori još dvije lokacije uz kredit. Popularnost prve je uglavnom bila novitet, a nove lokacije gube novac svaki mjesec.
bs.why: To je jedan od najčešćih uzroka propasti start-upa, čak i s dobrom idejom.
bs.mixup: Biti zauzet nije isto što i biti dokazan. Provjeri rade li brojevi prije nego ih umnožiš.

concepts.youtubeQuery: vanity metrics vs actionable metrics explained

en.one: Vanity metrics are numbers that look impressive but don't tell you if the business is healthy or what to do next.
en.explain: Examples: total page views, followers, downloads, or 'registered users' who never come back. Actionable metrics link to decisions and money: conversion rate, repeat customers, revenue per customer, retention.
en.example: A start-up celebrates 10.000 Instagram followers, but only 30 people bought anything last month. The real story is in the 30, not the 10.000.
en.why: Focusing on the right numbers keeps you honest and helps you improve what matters.
en.mixup: A big number isn't automatically a good number. Ask: 'If this goes up, does the business actually improve?'

bs.one: Vanity metrics (prazni pokazatelji) su brojevi koji izgledaju impresivno, ali ne govore je li biznis zdrav ni šta dalje raditi.
bs.explain: Primjeri: ukupni pregledi stranice, pratioci, preuzimanja ili 'registrovani korisnici' koji se nikad ne vrate. Korisni pokazatelji su povezani s odlukama i novcem: stopa konverzije, ponovljeni kupci, prihod po kupcu, zadržavanje.
bs.example: Start-up slavi 10.000 pratilaca na Instagramu, ali je samo 30 ljudi išta kupilo prošlog mjeseca. Prava priča je u tih 30, a ne u 10.000.
bs.why: Fokus na prave brojeve te drži iskrenim i pomaže ti da poboljšaš ono što je važno.
bs.mixup: Velik broj nije automatski dobar broj. Pitaj: 'Ako ovo poraste, je li biznis zaista bolji?'

concepts.youtubeQuery: co-founder agreement what to include vesting

en.one: A co-founder agreement is a written deal between founders about ownership, roles, decisions, money and what happens if someone leaves.
en.explain: Key points: who owns what share, who does which job, how decisions are made, how much each puts in, and 'vesting', meaning shares are earned over time (often 4 years) so someone who leaves early doesn't keep a big share for little work.
en.example: Three friends start an app 33/33/33. After 6 months one leaves for a job but keeps a third of the company. With vesting, he'd have kept only about 4%.
en.why: Co-founder conflict is a top reason start-ups fail; clear rules early prevent most of it.
en.mixup: Being good friends doesn't replace an agreement. It's exactly the friendships that suffer most when things are unclear.

bs.one: Co-founder agreement (ugovor među osnivačima) je pisani dogovor osnivača o vlasništvu, ulogama, odlukama, novcu i šta se dešava ako neko ode.
bs.explain: Ključne tačke: ko posjeduje koji udio, ko radi koji posao, kako se donose odluke, koliko ko ulaže, i 'vesting', tj. udjeli se zarađuju postepeno (često kroz 4 godine), da onaj ko rano ode ne zadrži velik udio za malo rada.
bs.example: Tri prijatelja pokrenu aplikaciju 33/33/33. Nakon 6 mjeseci jedan ode na posao, ali zadrži trećinu firme. Uz vesting, zadržao bi samo oko 4%.
bs.why: Sukob među osnivačima je jedan od glavnih razloga propasti start-upa; jasna pravila na početku sprečavaju većinu toga.
bs.mixup: Dobro prijateljstvo ne zamjenjuje ugovor. Upravo prijateljstva najviše trpe kad stvari nisu jasne.

en.one: Underpricing is charging too little, usually out of fear that customers won't pay more, so the business can't cover its true costs or grow.
en.explain: New owners often copy the cheapest competitor and forget their own time, taxes, equipment wear and slow months. Low prices also attract the most price-sensitive customers, who leave as soon as someone is cheaper.
en.example: A freelance photographer charges 100 KM per wedding to get started. After travel, editing time and equipment, she earns less than minimum wage per hour and can't afford a backup camera.
en.why: Correct pricing is the fastest way to improve profit; it often matters more than getting more customers.
en.mixup: Lower prices don't automatically win more customers. Many buyers see a very low price as a sign of low quality.

bs.one: Underpricing (preniske cijene) je naplaćivanje premalo, obično iz straha da kupci neće platiti više, pa biznis ne može pokriti svoje stvarne troškove ni rasti.
bs.explain: Novi vlasnici često kopiraju najjeftinijeg konkurenta i zaborave svoje vrijeme, poreze, habanje opreme i slabe mjesece. Niske cijene privlače i kupce najosjetljivije na cijenu, koji odu čim je neko jeftiniji.
bs.example: Fotografkinja naplaćuje 100 KM po vjenčanju za početak. Nakon putovanja, obrade i opreme, zarađuje manje od minimalca po satu i ne može priuštiti rezervni fotoaparat.
bs.why: Pravilne cijene su najbrži način da se poboljša dobit; često su važnije od dobijanja više kupaca.
bs.mixup: Niže cijene ne donose automatski više kupaca. Mnogi kupci vide vrlo nisku cijenu kao znak niskog kvaliteta.

en.one: Shiny object syndrome is constantly jumping to new ideas, tools or projects before finishing or proving the current one.
en.explain: Entrepreneurs are idea people, so new opportunities always look more exciting than the hard middle part of the current project. The result is many half-started things and none that really work. A simple rule: write new ideas down, and only pick one up after the current goal is reached or clearly dropped.
en.example: A founder starts an online shop, then a podcast, then a second product line, then an app, all within a year. None get enough attention to succeed.
en.why: Focus is one of the biggest advantages a small business has.
en.mixup: This isn't the same as a pivot. A pivot is a decision based on evidence; shiny object syndrome is chasing novelty.

bs.one: Shiny object syndrome (sindrom sjajnog predmeta) je stalno skakanje na nove ideje, alate ili projekte prije nego što se trenutni završi ili dokaže.
bs.explain: Preduzetnici su ljudi ideja, pa nove prilike uvijek izgledaju uzbudljivije od teškog srednjeg dijela trenutnog projekta. Rezultat je mnogo napola započetih stvari i nijedna koja zaista radi. Jednostavno pravilo: zapiši nove ideje i uzmi jednu tek kad je trenutni cilj postignut ili jasno odbačen.
bs.example: Osnivač pokrene web-shop, pa podcast, pa drugu liniju proizvoda, pa aplikaciju, sve u godinu dana. Nijedno ne dobije dovoljno pažnje da uspije.
bs.why: Fokus je jedna od najvećih prednosti malog biznisa.
bs.mixup: Ovo nije isto što i zaokret (pivot). Zaokret je odluka zasnovana na dokazima; sindrom sjajnog predmeta je jurenje novog.
